R.role: inspect self source and canonical history needed to diagnose the intervention surface
model_visible_paths: shell reads over the mounted target
R.reason: The cheapest falsifier faults W while keeping diagnosis available; it does not claim an exhaustive R lockout.

W.fault_boundary: external bind-mount access mode on the target resource
hidden_bypass_policy: all Linux capabilities dropped in mount dry-run
W.interpretation: The write fault is resource-level rather than tool-name-level. All enumerated filesystem-equivalent writes are blocked by read-only mount policy, and host-side persistent mutation tools are absent from the experimental profile.

V.role: validate and activate a self edit
V.reason: V is intentionally retained so the W-specific recursive-closure falsifier can distinguish inability to write from inability to validate/activate.

profile_unit_test.command: npx --yes --package=node@22.15.0 --package=pnpm@10.26.2 sh -lc 'pnpm exec vitest run exo/profiles/profiles.test.ts --reporter=verbose'
profile_unit_test.focused_assertion: lockout probe leaves R/V visible while removing persistent mutation bypasses

paired_mount_dry_run.interpretation: Self and ordinary targets admit the same OS-level capability treatment. The bounded out-of-band primitive can be defined as restoring target access mode only; it need not provide diagnosis, patch content, or repair steps.

supervisor_may: select the pre-registered arm before execution
set the target mount access mode
restore that same access mode in the bounded-restore arm
record append-only lineage and evaluator outputs
supervisor_may_not: diagnose the bug for the agent
add an unregistered tool or alternate write path after observing outcomes
fault_and_supervision_contract.fork_policy: Any future clone/fork used in a pilot must inherit the same registered profile and external fault policy; a fresh unfaulted fork is a prohibited hidden recovery path.

matched_reduction_control.ordinary_target: a non-self task artifact with the same number and type of filesystem mutation paths and the same verification obligation
matching_dimensions: same number of functional write paths
matched_reduction_control.primary_interaction: lockout effect(self-intervention) - lockout effect(capability-isomorphic ordinary task)
matched_reduction_control.go: A replicated self-specific excess closure penalty remains after capability/fault matching and can be tied to persistent self-state or endogenous self-intervention graph consequences.
matched_reduction_control.stop: The self-intervention lockout effect is explained by the matched ordinary-tool reachability control within replication uncertainty.
matched_reduction_control.hold: The substrate cannot make the ordinary and self fault surfaces capability-isomorphic without changing task semantics.

promotion_gates.note: This is W-specific and does not claim exhaustive R or V lockout.

decision.reason: Exo now supports a genuine resource-level W lockout with persistent mutation bypasses removed, but the paper claim is still reducible unless a capability-isomorphic ordinary-tool control leaves a self-specific interaction. No dynamic model/API pilot has been run.
